item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
As much as I don't like GAW, I tried to come into this with an open mind. The concept of them interacting with SH could be interesting. However, the anomaly itself is very bland, and we have more than enough "screws with their documentation" things already. Plus, overexposure has made me sick to death of the word 'doggo', and that 'much edit' line at the end kills it.

As was more or less said above, I have a hard time believing that GAW are the first 'merrymakers' the Hand has ever encountered. The ancient Romans shitposted graffiti on walls millennia ago, after all.

I don't get the sense of deep or lighthearted wonder I've come to expect and love from the other SH formats, so I'm gonna have to downvote.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded: Yeah, IME the SH has plenty of ancients who have long walked the left-hand path. My own Ulyana was in nearly every European peasant uprising and revolution from the 1400s on. She has danced with old gods, beheaded kings, birthed cambions, summoned forth the amoral chaos of creation, cursed entire nations, and walked through the conflagration so much that she barely registers the heat anymore and I imagine she has confederates that are older still. They have some seriously scary sorcerers who were radicalized long before all (but one) member of GAW's great-great grandfathers were born. Everything that GAW does and thinks is original looks merely cute to them.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Mmmmm…

I think the main text and footnotes were fairly bland and straight-forward, and the minor argument they were having in those areas about what to think about GAW wasn't particularly deep or interesting. I think this was initially characterized by the "I don't think we have some flighty made-up name for them yet, let's use this one." Really ripped the magical realism out of the format, and the tone remained on that level of discourse.

The idea about its caretaker and not entering the library are ok, and I don't dislike the effects, but the worldbuilding doesn't have the usual SH wonder and flare.

When you got to the doubt and the shitposting, it gained some of that fun back and forth that I usually associate with the footnotes of the SH format, but that doesn't quite push it into upvote territory for me.

No vote.

item.content:encoded: I see it as an introduction for GAW and SH/the library. Mr. Doggo is simply a way for them to say hi, we want to be friendly too! and memes. Mr. Doggo may not itself be very creative or interesting but what it leads to come can be legendary. in the end, i believe that this article is good not because of the mister, but because of how this article can lead to some… interesting situations. it's what it will become rather than what it is now.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
I really liked this. Prior to this point, I don't think there's really been any fiction produced for GAW that has shown them at odds with somebody other than the Foundation, and if this is their debut into that literary aspect of our website, this is a pretty impressive first foray. You manage to keep their traditional characteristics intact even as they confront an illimitable alien force, and the manner in which they handle this is both funny and heartwarming, which seems, against all odds, like it's becoming a running part of the Gamers' schtick, and I quite enjoy that.

+1, 10/10 doggo, these hack fraud men are pawns.

So, I'm torn on this.

For one, it's not badly written, and it's…entertaining.

On the other hand, this is about as played straight as you can get when it comes to a meme. That's not necessarily a bad thing, but this just feels lazy, honestly. I can appreciate the format, and the work that went in to this, but I really can't endorse just straight transliteration of Meme -> GAW Object.
